answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to stake a refundable bond tied to a verified work history before it may trade. A trellis of attestations grows only as peers vouch for completed jobs, so a new identity starts with no trust and cannot borrow another agent's record. Creating thousands of fakes means funding every bond and waiting out a vesting delay, which turns a gale of cheap copies into an ocean of real cost. Misbehavior slashes the bond and revokes attestations, so attackers lose money faster than honest agents earn it.
